question: Annie Besant was a Fabian socialist under the influence of _________ .
solution:
The correct answer is __**George Bernard Shaw**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Annie Besant was a British socialist, theosophist, women's rights activist, writer, orator, educationist, and philanthropist.
 
• She was a prominent figure in the Fabian Society, a socialist organization in the United Kingdom.
 
• George Bernard Shaw, an Irish playwright and critic, was one of the founding members of the Fabian Society and had a significant influence on Annie Besant.
 
• The Fabian Society aimed at the establishment of a democratic socialist state in the United Kingdom through gradual and reformist means.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fabian Society**

 
 
• Established in 1884, the Fabian Society is a British socialist organization that aimed to advance the principles of democratic socialism via gradualist and reformist efforts rather than revolutionary means.
 
• It is associated with the Labour Party in the UK and was instrumental in the party's formation.
 
• The society's members, known as Fabians, have included prominent figures such as George Bernard Shaw, H.G. Wells, and Sidney and Beatrice Webb.
 
• The society's influence extended into the fields of politics, education, and social reform.
 
 
 
• **George Bernard Shaw**
 
 
• George Bernard Shaw (1856-1950) was an Irish playwright, critic, polemicist, and political activist.
 
• He was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1925 and is best known for his plays, including "Pygmalion" and "Man and Superman."
 
• Shaw was a co-founder of the London School of Economics and a member of the Fabian Society, where he advocated for gradual social reform and the establishment of a welfare state.
 
• His works and ideas had a significant influence on contemporary social and political thought.
 
 
 
• **Annie Besant**
 
 
• Annie Besant (1847-1933) was a prominent British socialist, theosophist, women's rights activist, writer, and orator.
 
• She became involved in the Indian independence movement and served as the president of the Indian National Congress in 1917.
 
• Besant was also influential in the Theosophical Society, where she worked to promote spiritual and educational reforms.
 
• Her contributions to social reform, education, and the fight for Indian independence remain significant in history.
